detail.longDescription:
Then I decided that I wanted macOS and Windows versions. This is where things get interesting. It’s also where the pain begins.

My initial Windows implementation was a batch file. I dunno, it seemed like a good idea at the time. The result is the most tortured batch file I’ve written. I did some things that I thought were clever, like using `%ERRORLEVEL%` to simulate function returns in a language that, strictly speaking, doesn’t have functions. I also structured it in a way more akin to a C/C++ program, main “function” and all, which is definitely not the usual batch file paradigm.

Much to my surprise and delight, it worked! I pulled it off. But there was a catch, and it wound up being deal-breaking in my case: I couldn’t run it in an MSYS2 environment. MSYS2 environments and batch files don’t mix.

I needed a different solution, and that brings me to the next part of this slightly unhinged journey.

https://github.com/digichelle/odctl-cmd
